editorial:
Imagine waking up on a cold New York City street with absolutely no idea who you are. That is exactly where you start with this story. You follow a confused man who has lost his memory and has to wander through Manhattan, talking to strangers and searching for any clue about his past. The vibe is very moody and mysterious, making you feel just as lost as the main character is. It feels like a puzzle where you get a few pieces at a time, and you will find yourself rooting for him to figure out his identity before someone else does.

The acting is top-notch and really sells the feeling of panic and confusion. While the story moves a bit slow at times, the payoff is worth the wait. If you like mysteries that focus more on a person's mind than big explosions, you will love this. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a remastered 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: You eventually find out that the main character is actually a wealthy man who tried to commit suicide because he was unhappy with his life. He survived but lost his memory. In the end, he realizes that the life he forgot was actually miserable. He decides he is better off starting over as a new person rather than going back to his old, sad identity. He chooses to leave his past behind and move forward into a fresh start.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and slow-burn mysteries.
